Package neqsim.process.equipment.valve

Class ValveRangeabilityScreening

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.valve.ValveRangeabilityScreening
public final class ValveRangeabilityScreening extends Object
Screening helper for control-valve installed-flow sensitivity at low travel.

A recycle / anti-surge valve is sometimes constrained to a minimum opening above its true desired setpoint (e.g. a positioner "low clamp" added to avoid seat wear or perceived instability). This helper quantifies, for a given ISA-75 style inherent trim characteristic and rangeability, how much extra flow such a forced minimum-opening clamp lets through relative to the desired opening - a first screening step before committing to a detailed valve signature test or a full process simulation of the resulting recompression power penalty. It performs no thermodynamics and no network or database access; it is pure ISA-75 trim-curve arithmetic.

  • Method Details

    • flowFraction

      public static double flowFraction(ValveTrimCharacteristic trim, double travelFraction, double rangeability)
      Normalized flow fraction (Cv/Cv_max) for the given trim characteristic at the given travel fraction and rangeability.
      Parameters:
      trim - trim characteristic
      travelFraction - travel fraction, 0-1 (values are clamped to this range)
      rangeability - rangeability (Cv_max / Cv_min), must be greater than 1
      Returns:
      normalized flow fraction, in [1/rangeability, 1] for LINEAR and EQUAL_PERCENTAGE, or [0, 1] for QUICK_OPENING
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if trim is null, inputs are non-finite, or rangeability is not greater than one

    • evaluate

      public static ValveRangeabilityScreening.Result evaluate(ValveTrimCharacteristic trim, double travelFraction1, double travelFraction2, double rangeability)
      Evaluate the extra flow passed at a second (typically forced/clamped) travel fraction relative to a first (typically desired) travel fraction, for the given ISA-75 style trim characteristic and rangeability.
      Parameters:
      trim - trim characteristic
      travelFraction1 - first (desired) travel fraction, 0-1
      travelFraction2 - second (actual/clamped) travel fraction, 0-1
      rangeability - rangeability (Cv_max / Cv_min), must be greater than 1 (typical control valves: 30-50)
      Returns:
      a ValveRangeabilityScreening.Result carrying both flow fractions and the resulting flow ratio
